category_definition: African Grocery Store: an independent retail storefront selling African pantry staples (fufu/poundo flour, gari, egusi, ogbono, teff flour, injera, berbere, suya spice, red palm oil, stockfish, bitter leaf, malt drinks), fresh/frozen tropical produce and proteins (yams, plantains, cassava leaves, halal goat/mutton/cow foot), African health-and-beauty products, and related specialty goods. Subcategories observed in this market: West African (Nigerian, Ghanaian, Senegalese, Liberian), East African/Habesha (Ethiopian/Eritrean), Somali/East African halal markets with remittance counters, pan-African/Caribbean hybrids, and large international supermarkets with substantial African sections (probable fit only). Business model is product-first retail, frequently hybridized with cooked-food counters, halal butchery, remittance/mobile top-up agency (MoneyGram, Dahabshil), direct-import supply chains, or African textiles. Restaurants without a retail grocery component (e.g., Abyssinia, Axum, Zara Habesha, Barako Somali, Barry's African Restaurant, Lete's Injera and Cafe, The Jollof Buka, Eko African Cuisine) were excluded from the qualifying set.
geographic_classification_notes: inside_city was assigned to all Marion County / Indianapolis addresses across the swept corridors (Lafayette Rd, Georgetown Rd, W 38th St, E 38th St, W Morris St, W Washington St, Rockville Rd, Madison Ave, W 22nd St, N/S High School Rd, Girls School Rd, W 10th St, N Keystone Ave, E Thompson Rd, St Peter St, S Lynhurst Dr, E Troy Ave). Nhyira International Market (Greenwood, Johnson County) is inside the Indianapolis MSA and classified metro_area. Saraga's three locations (Westside, Castleton, Greenwood/Stop 11) are consolidated into one local_chain record with the Westside flagship address; all three are within Indianapolis city limits. Enerem African Food Store (Huntertown, Allen County - Fort Wayne area) and Blessing International Market (Columbus, Bartholomew County) are outside the Indianapolis MSA and classified outside_market; both are excluded from the qualifying set per discovery scope. Batis African Store's registry lists both a Camby (Decatur Township) and an Indianapolis address; the Indianapolis address governs. Supplement added 11 additional inside_city candidates (Rachel, Tetee, Arsema, Grace, Godbless, Golden Crown, Victory, 22nd Street, Baobab, Hana, Rachel International).
ownership_exclusion_notes: No national_chain, national_franchise, or regional_chain entities were identified in this market. Saraga International Grocery is the only multi-location operator (3 Indianapolis-metro locations plus Columbus, OH) and is retained as local_chain; per emerging-focus rules it is kept as established-leader reference context with business_seek_recommended=false rather than promoted into the emerging prospect set. All other records are single-location independents. Four registry-only entities (Jackieline African Market, Batis African Store, Joshoua Africa Market, African Food Services) have no verifiable storefront evidence and are held with category_fit=insufficient. African Caribbean Market is held due to an unresolved current-business-status conflict (LLC voluntarily dissolved; two historical addresses; no recent operational evidence). All 11 supplement candidates are also independent operators.

outreach_recommendation.platform_rationale: Google Business Profile is where the gold standard is deepest (20 expected photos, full NAP+hours+website+description gates) AND where the most candidates have fixable gaps. The vast majority of the 45 combined candidates have no functional website and no confirmed GBP. SNAP registry and INBiz were the actual discovery surfaces for the thinnest candidates, but these are not outreach platforms.

platform_specific_opportunities.opportunity: 45 candidates with the majority missing claimed/complete GBP — all are GBP claim and completion opportunities
platform_specific_opportunities.evidence_summary: Arsema G Food Mart has 2025 customs import manifests and SNAP authorization but zero public web presence. Grace Variety Store has owner-named reviews confirming Nigerian grocery specialization but no GBP. Jokkymore has 30 reviews on Restaurantji but no owned website. All are high-value GBP claim targets.

platform_specific_opportunities.opportunity: Only 1 candidate (Ethiopian Market) has a BBB record — BBB listing creation is a differentiation opportunity for the other 44
platform_specific_opportunities.evidence_summary: Ako International Market (Tempe) is the BBB benchmark in the gold standard. Ethiopian Market is miscategorized under Restaurants on BBB. Arsema and Grace are strong enough to warrant BBB profiles.

platform_specific_opportunities.opportunity: Most candidates have no confirmed Yelp presence — hidden-trust-to-visible-trust conversion
platform_specific_opportunities.evidence_summary: Yelp benchmark (Accra African International Market) shows 5.0/5 with community storytelling. Grace Variety Store has equivalent community trust in food-us.org reviews but no Yelp presence.

outreach_recommendation.primary_angle: You are authorized to accept SNAP/EBT and serve the African diaspora community — we can help customers find your store, hours, and SNAP acceptance on Google.
outreach_recommendation.suggested_call_to_action: Claim your free Google Business Profile so customers can find your store, see your hours, and know you accept EBT.
